subject: Re: Appendix A - Commissioning pricing schedule and minimum/maximum tiers
content:
From: Han Lee <han.lee@greenwavehealth.com>
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com; rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@greenwavehealth.com; Sophie Turner <sophie.turner@legalpartners.io>
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Appendix A - Commissioning pricing schedule and minimum/maximum tiers

Marissa / Rishi,

Thanks for the draft order form — overall looks good. A couple of items our procurement/legal team flagged on Appendix A (pricing schedule):

- We need clarification on the monthly spending cap language. Your current draft ties a "soft cap" to throughputs which makes committing difficult for budgeting. Can you provide a numeric cap/ceiling by month for the dedicated pool?
- The minimum annual commitment (floor) in Exhibit A seems high relative to our expected pilot. Will Redwood accept a scaled floor for Year 1 (50% of the committed units) with a true-up at renewal?
- We also have a request to move any pricing caps/floors language out of the Master Services Agreement and into Appendix A so it's independently negotiable. Sophie (copied) will circulate a proposed redline.

If you can share a counter on the cap/floor structure and confirm whether you can include a 30-day overage window before throttling, we can get legal to review quickly.

Best,
Han
Head of Platform Integrations
GreenWave Health

---

On Tue, Jun 16, 2026 at 11:03 AM marissa_cole@redwood.com wrote:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Han Lee <han.lee@greenwavehealth.com>
Cc: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com; procurement@greenwavehealth.com
Date: Tue, 16 Jun 2026 11:03:21 -0700
Subject: Re: Appendix A - Commissioning pricing schedule and minimum/maximum tiers

Han — thanks for the concrete asks. Quick thoughts below, and I attached a numeric counterproposal for Appendix A.

- Monthly cap: we can set an explicit dollar ceiling per month tied to the dedicated pool for the first 12 months. Proposed ceiling: $120,000/month for the dedicated pool (we can revisit at renewal).
- Year 1 floor: we can support a 50% scaled floor for the pilot (applies to committed units only). The remaining 50% would be billed as on-demand at the same tiered rates, with a true-up at contract year end.
- Appendix placement: we prefer caps/floors in Appendix A (agree with your request). We'll make that change in the redline.
- Overage window: we can include a 30-day grace window before throttling but require overages to be billed at the agreed overage rate.

I've attached "GreenWave_Pricing_Counter_20260617.xlsx" with per-1K token tiers, example month-by-month spend, and the proposed $120k cap illustration. We left the uplift discount at 18% on the 3-tier committed banding — if they need deeper discount we will need either a longer commit term or a higher minimum.

Proposing a short call tomorrow to walk the schedule with Sophie and procurement. Thoughts?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: GreenWave_Pricing_Counter_20260617.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB)

Attaching our redline to Appendix A. Key commercial/legal items we pushed back on:

1) Ambiguous cap mechanism — redline proposes a fixed monthly dollar cap and an annual true-up clause.
2) Floor reduction — we requested the 50% Year 1 floor language be explicit and include a measurement window for true-up timing.
3) Billing / invoice credits — redline asks for credits for unconsumed committed units in a narrow set of circumstances (force majeure, platform unavailability > 48 hours).

Rishi / Grace — looping you both for quick internal alignment before I reply to GreenWave's redline. Summary of asks: numeric monthly ceiling ($120k proposed), 50% Year 1 floor request (agree in principle), move caps/floors into Appendix A (we agree), and credits for long outages (need to check SLAs).

Questions for Rishi: is $120k/month acceptable from margin / capacity planning perspective for the Dedicated pool? If not, what alternatives do we present? Also, any concerns with the proposed true-up timing Sophie suggested?

Grace — can you run the outage credit language vs. our standard SLA? They want credits where platform unavailable >48h; our standard window is 72h for significant credits. We should be careful about opening a 48h exposure.

I'll keep the counter spreadsheet light on discount until we confirm floor/cap. Want to preserve ability to request a longer term for deeper discount.

Thanks,
Marissa

Date: Wed, 17 Jun 2026 11:34:09 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Appendix A - Commissioning pricing schedule and minimum/maximum tiers

Marissa — $120k/month is borderline for the pool size they want in Q1 but workable if we: (a) lock the commit term to 12 months, and (b) include a soft tier that lets us scale up at pre-agreed incremental unit pricing. If they insist on Year 1 50% floor and a flexible monthly cap we should require a 10% higher overage rate and a 12-month minimum term.

On the SLA credit: agree with Grace that moving to a 72h window reduces risk. If GreenWave pushes back we can offer a limited exception for the pilot period only.

I'll propose language: "Year 1 pilot floor = 50% of annual committed units billed monthly; any shortfall will be billed as on-demand and subject to annual true-up. If GreenWave elects to reduce their committed level at renewal, standard ramp-down schedule applies."

Rishi
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
